timecoded_text_to_speech.text: In this lab you'll be looking at the evolution of carbon dioxide gas from metal
carbonate salts. This will be done by measuring the mass of the solid before and
after reaction with a strong acid. You will start this experiment by tearing the
bounds and weighing a clean and dry beaker and test tube. Record the mass in your
lab notebook. You will then take your given carbonate metal and add it to the
beaker. You'll want to add about 0.75 to 1.25 grams of the solid. You will need
about a quarter of a test tube full of sulfuric acid. You will find the sulfuric
acid in the fume wood. Carefully add it to the test tube and do not get any of it
into the beaker.
Record the mass of the beaker, test tube, acid and solid now that you've added
them all together. Once you have recorded the masses you may proceed with the
reaction. Pour all of the acid into the beaker with the carbonate solid. This will
cause the evolution of carbon dioxide gas. Be sure that all the metal carbonate has
reacted and that all the carbon dioxide has been driven out of the solution
swirl the beaker gently. If you notice that there is any of the solid on the
walls of the beaker tilt it carefully and rinse down the solid. Make sure it gets
dissolved by the acid.
Once the reaction is complete, re-way the beaker, test tube and solution. The
difference in mass is due to the carbon dioxide that has been driven out of the
solution.
